- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for rebound potential.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model often holds too high; apply downward bias of 2–4% for next 3–5 periods.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1.00, -0.00, 1.00), model tends to misalign horizon — use sentiment-weighted smoothing: average recent 3–5 days’ sentiment to adjust forecast direction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently 5–10% below model, apply “mean reversion bias” — subtract 2–5% from forecast for next 5–7 periods.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often misses momentum — add 1–2% to forecast to capture hidden momentum.
